item.title: On the campaign trail, Trump delivers his greatest political hits and mourns end of rallies
item.description: President Trump is campaigning hard in the midterms. Supporters are showing up, in part because this could be the last chance to see him holding the large rallies that have been his trademark.
item.content:encoded: President Trump is campaigning hard in the midterms. Supporters are showing up, in part because this could be the last chance to see him holding the large rallies that have been his trademark.
item.dc:creator: Tamara Keith

item.title: Fishing is a key issue in Alaska's tight U.S. Senate race
item.description: Alaska's U.S. Senate race is embroiled in an emotional fight over fish. Many in the state rely upon salmon to feed their families but those fish and others are increasingly hard to find.
item.content:encoded: Alaska's U.S. Senate race is embroiled in an emotional fight over fish. Many in the state rely upon salmon to feed their families but those fish and others are increasingly hard to find.

item.title: GDP report to give insight before Election Day. And, Israel's election is deadlocked
item.description: Economists expect the GDP report to show economic growth, but say that growth is "fragile." And, after 90% of the votes in Israel have been counted, no clear winner has emerged.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: These are the House races to watch in the 2026 midterm election on Nov. 3
item.description: An NPR analysis finds 70 House districts where Democrats and Republicans are each investing more than six figures in advertising during the final few days of the election, including in deep red areas.

item.title: Support for Trump among white evangelicals has plummeted, polls reveal
item.description: Three new polls suggest that President Trump is losing ground among white evangelicals. What explains this drop — and will it affect the midterm elections?

item.title: Hackers expose the identities of more than 40,000 DHS employees
item.description: A group of hacktivists calling themselves Distributed Denial of Secrets, said the unmasking of ICE agents, DHS operatives and contractors was fair play, given the government's lack of transparency.

item.title: Judge denies the Justice Department's bid to stop processing California ballots
item.description: While the judge rejected the Department of Justice's unprecedented demand in California, the case isn't over yet. The federal government immediately filed notice that it will appeal.

item.title: Israel's election too close to call. And, the Ebola outbreak reaches grim milestone
item.description: Israeli voters turned out in record numbers, and the results remain too close to call. And, more than 10,000 people have been infected with Ebola since the outbreak was first declared in May.
